newsitem.title: USA: Abbott asthma drug cleared by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Abbott asthma drug cleared by FDA.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared its Zyflo drug as a treatment of chronic asthma and to prevent asthma symptoms in patients aged 12 years and older.
Abbott said Zyflo inhibits the formation of leukotrienes, which contribute to the inflammation and swelling of the airways and increased mucus secretion in patients with asthma.
"By inhibiting formation of leukotrienes, Zyflo helps control asthma symptoms," Andre Pernet, Abbott vice president of pharmaceutical research, said in a statement.

In clinical trials involving patients with mild to moderate asthma who used inhaled prescription medication, Zyflo decreased the percentage of patients who needed steriod treatments for asthma attacks.
In addition, patients taking Zyflow were able to reduce their use of inhaled medication in general.
Abbott said Zyflo should not be used to treat acute episodes of asthma.
Zyflo will be available nationwide by prescription in January, Abbott said.
